# Architectural vs. 3-tab shingles: what's the difference?
The two main types of asphalt shingles, and why most roofers now quote architectural.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: 3-tab shingles are thin, flat, single-layer shingles with a uniform look. Architectural (also called dimensional or laminated) shingles are made of two or more bonded layers, so they're thicker, have a textured look, usually carry higher wind ratings and longer warranties, and cost somewhat more. Most new residential roofs in the U.S. now use architectural shingles, and some manufacturers have reduced or discontinued 3-tab lines.

## Side-by-side
 | 3-tab | Architectural | 

Construction | Single layer | Two or more laminated layers | 

Look | Flat, uniform rows | Dimensional, shadowed, can mimic wood shake or slate | 

Weight | Lighter | Heavier | 

Wind rating | Often lower | Often higher | 

Typical life | Shorter | Longer | 

Price | Lowest | Somewhat higher | 

## When 3-tab still makes sense

- Repairing an existing 3-tab roof so patches match.
- Sheds, garages or rentals where the lowest price matters most.

## Beyond architectural
"Designer" or luxury shingles are heavier still and mimic slate or shake. Class 4 impact-resistant versions are available in many architectural lines. See Class 4 shingles and all roofing materials.

## Related guides
Roofing materials comparedMetal roof vs. asphalt shingles: which is better?Are Class 4 impact-resistant shingles worth it?How long does a roof last?

## Frequently asked questions

### Are architectural shingles worth the extra cost?
For most homeowners, yes: better wind resistance, a longer warranty and better curb appeal for a modest price difference on a full roof.

### Can you mix 3-tab and architectural shingles?
On separate roof sections, sometimes, but they look different side by side. For repairs, roofers try to match the existing type.

### How can I tell which shingles I have?
3-tab shingles show evenly spaced cutouts and a flat look. Architectural shingles look layered and uneven, with no regular tabs.

### Do architectural shingles need special installation?
They follow the manufacturer's nailing pattern like any shingle; the key is a crew that installs to spec so the warranty applies.

# Wind mitigation inspections: how they can lower your insurance
Common in Florida and other hurricane-prone areas, a wind mitigation inspection documents the features that help your home resist wind.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: A wind mitigation inspection documents how well your home's roof and openings resist hurricane winds. In Florida, insurers are required by law to offer discounts for qualifying wind-resistant features, and the inspection is usually recorded on the state's standard form (OIR-B1-1802). A new roof installed to current code, with the right nailing, secondary water barrier and roof-to-wall connections, can improve your results.

## What the inspector checks

- Roof covering and whether it meets current building code, with permit date.
- Roof deck attachment: nail size and spacing holding the decking to the rafters.
- Roof-to-wall attachment: toe nails, clips, single or double wraps (hurricane straps).
- Roof shape: hip roofs generally score better than gable roofs.
- Secondary water resistance: a sealed roof deck under the covering.
- Opening protection: impact windows, doors and shutters.

## Who does it
Licensed home inspectors, contractors, engineers and other professionals allowed by your state. Fees vary; ask before booking.

## Timing with a new roof
If you're replacing your roof, ask the roofer about upgrades that affect the report, such as sealing the deck and re-nailing the decking to current code. Then get a new inspection after the permit passes and send it to your insurer.

More: Florida roofers and licensing and after storm damage.

## Related guides
What to do after storm damageHow to file a roof insurance claim, step by stepDo you need a permit to replace your roof?Old roof and home insurance: what to know

## Frequently asked questions

### How much can a wind mitigation inspection save?
It depends on your insurer, home and features found. Some homeowners see meaningful savings on the windstorm portion of their premium; others see little change.

### How long is a wind mitigation report valid?
In Florida, insurers generally accept the report for up to five years, as long as nothing material changes. Check with your insurer.

### Do I need a wind mitigation inspection outside Florida?
Some insurers in other coastal states offer similar discounts, such as for roofs built to FORTIFIED standards. Ask your agent.

### Does a new roof automatically lower my premium?
Not automatically. Send your insurer the permit and, where applicable, an updated wind mitigation report.

# Should you replace your roof before going solar?
Solar panels can last 25 years or more. If your roof won't, plan ahead.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: If your roof is more than about halfway through its expected life, or a roofer finds problems, it's usually smarter to replace it before installing solar. Solar panels commonly last 25 years or more, and removing and reinstalling them later for a roof replacement adds cost and hassle. Get a roof inspection first, and coordinate the roofer and solar installer so penetrations and flashing are done right.

## Why it matters

- Panels cover much of the roof, making later repairs harder.
- Detach-and-reset of panels for a reroof is a separate, often significant expense.
- Some solar warranties cover roof penetrations only if the roof was in good shape.

## How to decide

- Find your roof's age and material. See how long roofs last.
- Get a roof inspection and a written opinion on remaining life.
- If replacement is likely within the next several years, do it first.

## Coordinating the two jobs

- Ask whether the solar installer or roofer will flash the mounts, and who warranties leaks.
- Consider durable materials under the array, like architectural shingles or metal.
- Keep records of both warranties together.

## Related guides
How long does a roof last?What happens during a roof inspection?Metal roof vs. asphalt shingles: which is better?How to pay for a new roof: financing options

## Frequently asked questions

### How old is too old for a roof before solar?
There's no single cutoff, but many installers want a roof with at least as much remaining life as the panel warranty or plan for replacement first. An inspection gives a better answer than age alone.

### Does installing solar damage the roof?
Properly installed mounts are flashed and sealed. Leaks usually trace back to poor installation, so choose an installer with a workmanship warranty.

### Can I bundle roof replacement into solar financing?
Some solar companies and lenders allow it. Compare the total cost and terms with separate financing.

### Is metal roofing good for solar?
Yes. Standing seam metal allows clamp-on mounts without penetrations and outlasts most panels.

Homeowner guide

# Old roof and home insurance: what to know
Insurers pay close attention to roof age. Here's how it can affect your policy and your options.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: As a roof ages, many insurers charge more, switch roof coverage from replacement cost to actual cash value (which deducts for depreciation), require an inspection, or decline to renew the policy. Rules vary by insurer and state. If you get a notice about your roof, ask exactly what the insurer needs, get an independent inspection, and compare other insurers before replacing a roof that still has useful life.

## What insurers may do

- Raise premiums or deductibles for older roofs.
- Pay actual cash value (ACV) for the roof instead of replacement cost (RCV). See ACV vs RCV.
- Require a roof inspection or a roof certification.
- Non-renew the policy. Many states require advance written notice.

## What you can do

- Read the notice carefully and ask what would satisfy the insurer.
- Get a roof inspection with photos and an estimate of remaining life.
- Ask an independent agent to shop other carriers.
- If you replace the roof, send the permit and invoice to your insurer, and ask about discounts.
- Contact your state insurance department if you think a notice doesn't follow state rules.

## Related guides
Does insurance cover roof replacement?How to file a roof insurance claim, step by stepWhat happens during a roof inspection?9 signs you might need a new roof

## Frequently asked questions

### Can my insurance company drop me because of my roof's age?
In many states, insurers can decline to renew based on roof age or condition, usually with advance notice. Some states have added limits. Check your state insurance department's rules.

### What age roof do insurers consider old?
It varies by insurer and material. Asphalt shingle roofs past roughly 15 to 20 years often get extra scrutiny.

### Will insurance pay for a new roof if mine is old?
Only if a covered event, like hail or wind, caused damage. Wear and age aren't covered, and older roofs may be paid at actual cash value.

### Does a roof certification help?
It can. A certification or inspection report showing remaining life may satisfy some insurers or buyers.

Homeowner guide

# Emergency roof tarping after storm damage
After a storm opens up your roof, a tarp buys time and limits water damage until repairs.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: If storm damage lets water in, an emergency tarp can prevent much bigger interior damage. Most homeowner policies expect you to take reasonable steps to prevent further damage, and many cover the cost of emergency tarping as part of a covered claim. Climbing a damaged, wet roof is dangerous, so hire a roofer or emergency service when you can. Keep photos and receipts.

## Right after the storm

- Stay safe. Stay off the roof in wind, rain or darkness, and watch for downed power lines.
- Photograph damage outside and inside before anything is moved.
- Catch water inside with buckets and move belongings.
- Call a roofer or tarping service, and call your insurer to start a claim.

## How a proper tarp is installed

- A heavy-duty tarp extending well past the damaged area, ideally over the ridge so water runs off.
- Fastened with wood battens screwed or nailed through the tarp's edges, not just weighed down with bricks.
- Edges sealed so wind can't get under it.

## How long a tarp lasts
A tarp is temporary. Sun and wind wear it down, so schedule permanent repairs as soon as possible. After hurricanes, some areas have free federal or local temporary roofing programs; check official announcements.

More: storm damage guide and filing a claim.

## Related guides
What to do after storm damageRoof leaking? What to do right nowHow to file a roof insurance claim, step by stepRoofing scams and red flags

## Frequently asked questions

### Does insurance pay for an emergency roof tarp?
Often, as part of a covered claim, because policies expect you to prevent further damage. Keep the invoice and photos and check your policy.

### Can I tarp my roof myself?
It's possible on a low, dry, safe roof, but falls are a real risk. A roofer or tarping service is safer, especially on steep or wet roofs.

### How long can a roof tarp stay on?
It's meant to be temporary. Tarps degrade in sun and wind, so plan permanent repairs promptly.

### Should I sign with the company that tarps my roof?
You can hire a company to tarp without signing a full repair contract. Read anything carefully before signing, especially assignment-of-benefits forms.

URL: https://bedrockroof.com/roof-overlay-vs-tear-off/

Homeowner guide

# Roof overlay vs. tear-off: can you put new shingles over old?
An overlay (also called a layover or re-roof) saves tear-off work, but it isn't always allowed or wise.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: An overlay puts new shingles over one existing layer, which skips tear-off labor and disposal. It's only an option when the old roof is flat, dry and sound, and when local code allows it. Most U.S. codes, based on the International Residential Code, don't allow a new layer over two existing layers. A full tear-off costs more but lets the roofer inspect and repair the decking, and it's what most manufacturers and roofers prefer.

## Overlay vs. tear-off

 | Overlay | Tear-off | 

Up-front cost | Lower (no removal or dump fees) | Higher | 

Deck inspection | Hidden problems stay hidden | Rot and soft spots found and fixed | 

Underlayment, flashing, ice barrier | Often left as-is | Replaced with new | 

Weight | Adds a second layer of weight | One layer | 

Lifespan | Often shorter; old bumps telegraph through | Full lifespan of the new material | 

Next replacement | Two layers must come off | One layer | 

## When an overlay is a bad idea

- The roof already has two layers.
- The decking is soft, rotted or water-soaked, or the roof leaks in several places.
- The old shingles are badly curled or buckled, so the new ones won't lie flat.
- You live where ice dams form and need new ice-and-water barrier at the eaves.
- You're filing an insurance claim. Many claims pay for removal of the damaged roof, so an overlay leaves money and inspection on the table.

## Warranty and resale
Some shingle manufacturers limit or exclude warranty coverage for overlays, or offer their best warranties only on tear-offs. Read the specific warranty before you agree. Home buyers and inspectors may also ask how many layers a roof has. See roof warranties.

## What to ask your roofer

- How many layers are on the roof now?
- Does our city or county allow an overlay here?
- What does the shingle warranty say about overlays?
- Can you quote both options so I can compare?

## Related guides
What to expect during a roof replacementHow much does a roof replacement cost?Roof warranties explainedShould you repair or replace your roof?

## Frequently asked questions

### How many layers of shingles are allowed?
Most U.S. codes based on the International Residential Code allow at most two layers, so you can't add a new layer over two existing ones. Your local building department has the final say.

### Is an overlay cheaper?
Usually, because there's no tear-off labor or disposal. The savings can disappear if hidden deck damage causes problems later.

### Can metal roofing go over shingles?
Sometimes, with the right underlayment or furring strips and if code allows it. Many roofers still recommend a tear-off so the deck can be checked.

### Does an overlay void my warranty?
It depends on the manufacturer. Some reduce or exclude coverage for overlays. Read the warranty before you decide.

Homeowner guide

# Black streaks on your roof: algae, moss and lichen
Dark stains are common on shingle roofs in humid areas. Here's what they are and what to do.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Dark streaks on asphalt shingles are usually a type of algae, often called Gloeocapsa magma. It's mostly cosmetic. Moss and lichen are different: they hold moisture and can lift shingles, so they're worth removing. Clean gently with a roof-safe cleaner and low pressure, never a pressure washer. Algae-resistant shingles and zinc or copper strips near the ridge help prevent regrowth.

## What you're looking at

- Black or dark streaks running down the roof: algae. It grows on the shady, damp sides of the roof first.
- Green, fuzzy clumps: moss. It traps water and can push shingle edges up.
- Crusty, flat patches that cling tightly: lichen. Removing it by force can tear granules off.

## Does it damage the roof?
Algae is mostly a looks problem, although dark streaks can make a roof absorb a bit more heat. Moss and heavy lichen are a real concern because they hold moisture against the shingles and under their edges, which can shorten the roof's life and lead to leaks.

## How to clean it safely

- Hire a pro if the roof is steep, high or slippery. Wet, moss-covered roofs are dangerous.
- Use a cleaner made for roofs and follow the label. Shingle makers and roofing groups often suggest a diluted bleach solution or a commercial roof cleaner applied at low pressure.
- Rinse gently from the top down. Protect plants and keep runoff away from ponds and drains.
- Don't pressure wash or scrape. It strips granules, which protect shingles from the sun and can void warranties.
- Let dead moss loosen and fall off over time instead of prying it.

## Prevention

- Trim branches so the roof gets more sun and dries faster.
- Keep gutters and valleys clear of leaves.
- Zinc or copper strips near the ridge release metal ions in the rain that discourage growth.
- When you replace the roof, choose algae-resistant (AR) shingles, which contain copper granules.

## Related guides
9 signs you might need a new roofHow long does a roof last?What happens during a roof inspection?Roofing materials compared

## Frequently asked questions

### Are black streaks on my roof mold?
They're usually algae, not mold. It's mostly cosmetic but can be cleaned and prevented.

### Should I pressure wash my roof?
No. Pressure washing strips the protective granules from shingles and can void the warranty. Use a roof-safe cleaner at low pressure.

### Does homeowners insurance cover roof moss?
Generally no. Moss and algae are treated as maintenance, not sudden damage.

### Do I need a new roof because of moss?
Usually not, if it's caught early. Heavy moss that has lifted or rotted shingles may need repairs.

Homeowner guide

# Roof flashing: what it is and why it leaks
Many roof leaks start not in the shingles but at the flashing where the roof meets something else.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Flashing is thin metal (or sometimes rubber) that seals the joints where a roof meets a wall, chimney, skylight, vent pipe or valley. Those joints are where water most often gets in. Rusted, loose or poorly sealed flashing is one of the most common causes of leaks, and it can often be repaired without replacing the whole roof.

## Types of flashing

- Step flashing: L-shaped pieces woven in with each course of shingles where a roof meets a side wall.
- Counter flashing: set into a chimney or wall and lapped over the step flashing.
- Valley flashing: lines the valley where two roof slopes meet.
- Drip edge: metal along the eaves and rakes that guides water into the gutter and protects the deck edge.
- Pipe boots: collars around plumbing vents. Rubber boots crack in the sun over time.
- Skylight and chimney kits: pre-formed flashing for those openings.

## Signs of failing flashing

- Stains on the ceiling or wall near a chimney, skylight or where a roof meets a wall.
- Rust, gaps, or flashing that has pulled away.
- Caulk or roofing cement smeared over flashing as a quick fix, which often fails again.
- Cracked rubber around vent pipes.

## Repair or replace?
If the roof is in good shape, a roofer can usually replace the failing flashing or pipe boot on its own. If the roof is near the end of its life, it often makes sense to redo the flashing as part of a full replacement. Ask whether your quote includes new flashing rather than reusing old pieces. See repair or replace.

## Questions for your roofer

- Will you install new step and counter flashing, or reuse the old?
- Is drip edge included? Many codes now require it.
- What material are the pipe boots, and how long do they last?

## Related guides
Roof leaking? What to do right nowShould you repair or replace your roof?What happens during a roof inspection?How to read and compare roofing estimates

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the most common cause of roof leaks?
Failing flashing and cracked pipe boots are among the most common. Leaks tend to start where the roof meets something else.

### Can flashing be repaired without a new roof?
Often yes. A roofer can replace flashing or a pipe boot and weave in matching shingles if the rest of the roof is sound.

### Should old flashing be reused on a new roof?
Many roofers replace it, especially step flashing and drip edge, because old flashing can be bent or corroded. Ask what your quote includes.

### Is caulk enough to fix flashing?
Caulk or roofing cement is a short-term patch. A lasting fix is properly installed flashing.

Homeowner guide

# Roof underlayment: felt vs. synthetic, and why it matters
Underlayment is the layer between the roof deck and the shingles or metal. It's your backup when water gets past the top layer.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Underlayment is a water-resistant layer installed over the roof deck before shingles, metal or tile go on. Most new residential roofs today use synthetic underlayment, which is lighter, stronger and less prone to tearing than traditional asphalt felt. Self-adhering ice-and-water membrane is added at eaves, valleys and around openings, especially where ice dams or wind-driven rain are a risk.

## The main types

Type | What it is | Where it's used | 

Asphalt felt (#15 or #30) | Paper or fiberglass mat soaked in asphalt | Traditional; lower cost; can wrinkle when wet | 

Synthetic | Woven or spun polymer sheets | Most common on new roofs; lighter and tear-resistant | 

Self-adhering membrane (ice and water shield) | Rubberized asphalt with a sticky back that seals around nails | Eaves, valleys, around chimneys and skylights; whole-roof in some high-wind and coastal areas | 

## Why it matters

- It keeps the deck dry during installation.
- It's a second barrier if shingles blow off or water is driven under them.
- Some shingle warranties require specific underlayment products.
- Codes in cold climates often require ice barrier at the eaves, and some coastal areas encourage or require a sealed roof deck.

## What to look for in a quote

- The underlayment type and brand, not just "underlayment".
- Where ice-and-water membrane will go (eaves, valleys, around openings, or the whole roof).
- Whether it meets the shingle maker's requirements for the warranty you're being sold.

Compare quotes line by line with our guide to reading a roofing estimate.

## Related guides
How to read and compare roofing estimatesIce dams: what causes them and how to prevent themWhat to expect during a roof replacementRoofing materials compared

## Frequently asked questions

### Is synthetic underlayment better than felt?
For most new roofs, yes. It's lighter, stronger and resists tearing and wrinkling. Felt is cheaper and still meets code in many places.

### What is ice and water shield?
A self-adhering rubberized membrane that seals around nails. It goes at eaves, valleys and openings where water is most likely to back up.

### Do I need ice and water shield on the whole roof?
Not usually. It's commonly required at the eaves in cold climates. In some high-wind or coastal areas, a fully sealed deck is recommended.

### Can underlayment be replaced without new shingles?
No. It sits under the shingles, so replacing it means removing the roof covering.

Homeowner guide

# Tile roofs: clay vs. concrete, lifespan and repairs
Tile roofs are common in Florida, the Southwest and California. Here's what owners and buyers should know.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Clay and concrete tiles can last 50 years or more, and they resist fire and heat well. They cost more than shingles and are much heavier, so the framing must be able to carry them. On many tile roofs, the underlayment beneath the tiles wears out long before the tiles do, so a "tile roof replacement" sometimes means lifting the tiles, replacing the underlayment and putting the tiles back.

## Clay vs. concrete

 | Clay tile | Concrete tile | 

Look | Classic terracotta; color goes through the tile | Many shapes and colors; some colors fade over time | 

Weight | Heavy | Usually heavier than clay | 

Cost | Generally higher | Generally lower than clay | 

Lifespan | Often 50+ years | Often 40–50+ years | 

## Strengths and weak spots

- Strengths: long life, Class A fire ratings, good in heat, and a look many buyers want.
- Weak spots: tiles can crack if walked on or hit by large hail, and the underlayment underneath ages.

## Common repairs

- Replacing cracked or slipped tiles. Keep spare tiles from the original job if you can, since matching older tiles can be hard.
- Re-setting ridge and hip tiles.
- Fixing flashing at valleys and walls. See roof flashing.
- Lift-and-relay: removing tiles, installing new underlayment and reinstalling the tiles.

## Hiring for tile work
Not every roofer does tile. Ask how many tile roofs the crew has done, how they walk on the roof without cracking tiles, and whether the quote includes new underlayment and flashing. In hurricane areas, ask how the tiles will be fastened to meet local wind rules.

## Related guides
Roofing materials comparedHow long does a roof last?Roof underlayment: felt vs. synthetic, and why it mattersRoof flashing: what it is and why it leaks

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does a tile roof last?
The tiles often last 50 years or more. The underlayment beneath them usually needs replacing sooner, which can be done by lifting and relaying the tiles.

### Can you walk on a tile roof?
Carefully, and ideally only by an experienced roofer. Tiles can crack under weight if stepped on in the wrong place.

### Is tile more expensive than shingles?
Yes, tile generally costs more to buy and install, but it can last much longer.

### Can my house support a tile roof?
Tile is heavy. Switching from shingles to tile may need an engineer to confirm the framing can carry it.

Homeowner guide

# TPO vs. EPDM vs. PVC: which flat roof membrane is best?
The three most common single-ply membranes on U.S. commercial roofs, side by side.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: TPO is the most common choice on new low-slope commercial roofs. It's usually white and reflective, with heat-welded seams. EPDM is a rubber membrane with the longest track record, often used in colder climates and on buildings where cooling cost matters less. PVC costs more but resists grease and chemicals, so it's a common pick for restaurants and some industrial roofs. Installation quality, especially at seams, edges and penetrations, matters as much as which membrane you choose.

## Side by side

 | TPO | EPDM | PVC | 

Material | Thermoplastic polyolefin | Synthetic rubber | Polyvinyl chloride | 

Usual color | White (reflective) | Black (white available) | White (reflective) | 

Seams | Heat-welded | Taped or glued | Heat-welded | 

Grease and chemicals | Fair | Poor with oils and grease | Good | 

Typical fit | Warm and mixed climates; most new commercial roofs | Cold climates; budget-conscious owners | Restaurants, kitchens, some industrial uses | 

Relative cost | Moderate | Often lowest | Highest of the three | 

## How to choose

- Climate and energy: a white membrane reflects sunlight and can lower cooling loads in hot regions. Some local energy codes require a reflective ("cool") roof on low-slope commercial buildings.
- Roof traffic: if HVAC techs are on the roof often, ask about thicker membranes and walkway pads.
- Exhaust and grease: kitchen exhaust can damage EPDM and TPO; PVC or a protective pad near fans is common.
- Attachment: membranes can be mechanically fastened, fully adhered or ballasted. Wind exposure, deck type and budget decide which.
- Insulation: a replacement is often the time to add insulation under the membrane to meet current energy code.

## Questions for bidders

- What membrane thickness (mils) and attachment method are you quoting?
- Is this a manufacturer-warranted system, and for how many years?
- Will you remove the existing roof or recover over it, and did you take core samples to check for wet insulation?

More: flat roof types, roof coatings and commercial roofing.

## Related guides
Flat roof types comparedCommercial roofing: free inspections and quotesCommercial roof coatings: restore or replace?What drives commercial roof replacement cost?

## Frequently asked questions

### Is TPO better than EPDM?
Neither is best everywhere. TPO is reflective with welded seams and suits hot climates. EPDM has a long track record and suits colder climates and tighter budgets.

### Which flat roof membrane lasts longest?
Lifespans overlap and depend heavily on installation, thickness and maintenance. Ask each bidder what warranty term the manufacturer will issue for the exact system quoted.

### Why do restaurants use PVC roofs?
PVC resists grease and many chemicals better than TPO or EPDM, which matters near kitchen exhaust fans.

### Can a new membrane go over the old roof?
Sometimes. Codes usually limit the number of roof layers, and wet insulation must be removed first. Core samples or a moisture survey tell you what's under there.

Commercial roofing

# What drives commercial roof replacement cost?
Commercial roof prices vary widely, so it helps to know what's actually driving the number in each bid.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Commercial roofs are usually priced per square foot or per "square" (100 square feet), and the biggest drivers are the roof system, whether the old roof must be torn off, how much insulation is added, the building's height and access, and the warranty you want. Bids for the same building can differ a lot, so compare scope line by line rather than just the total. We don't publish a single average price, because it would be misleading across U.S. regions and building types.

## The main cost drivers

- Roof system: TPO, EPDM, PVC, modified bitumen, built-up, metal or a coating. See TPO vs EPDM vs PVC.
- Tear-off or recover: removing old layers costs more but finds wet insulation and deck damage. Codes limit how many layers you can have.
- Insulation: energy codes often require added insulation on a replacement, and tapered insulation fixes ponding water.
- Deck repairs: rusted metal deck or rotted wood is often priced per unit once exposed. Ask for those unit prices in the bid.
- Penetrations and details: HVAC curbs, drains, skylights, parapet walls and edge metal add labor.
- Access and height: cranes, hoists, street permits and working around tenants or business hours.
- Warranty level: a manufacturer's full system warranty usually requires specific materials and inspections, which can raise cost.

## How to compare bids

- Give every bidder the same scope, ideally in writing.
- Ask for core samples or an infrared or moisture survey so everyone prices the same conditions.
- Get unit prices for deck and insulation replacement.
- Confirm who pulls the permit and who handles HVAC disconnects.
- Check the contractor's license and insurance with your state. See choosing a roofer.

## Repair, coat or replace?
If the insulation is mostly dry and the membrane is sound, a repair or a restoration coating may extend the roof's life for less. Widespread wet insulation or repeated leaks usually mean replacement. Planned maintenance helps either way; see the maintenance checklist.

## Related guides
Commercial roofing: free inspections and quotesTPO vs. EPDM vs. PVC: which flat roof membrane is best?Commercial roof coatings: restore or replace?Commercial roof maintenance checklist

## Frequently asked questions

### How is commercial roofing priced?
Usually per square foot or per square (100 square feet), plus line items for tear-off, insulation, deck repairs, flashing and edge metal.

### Why are commercial roof bids so different?
Bidders often assume different scopes, such as recover vs tear-off, insulation thickness or warranty level. Give everyone the same written scope.

### Is a roof coating cheaper than replacement?
Usually, when the existing roof is sound and mostly dry. A coating won't fix wet insulation or a failing deck.

### Can roof replacement be deducted for a business?
Tax treatment of building improvements varies. Ask your accountant how a roof replacement is handled for your property.

Commercial roofing

# Commercial or flat roof leak: what to do first
Leaks on flat roofs are hard to trace because water travels. Here's how to respond quickly and in the right order.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Protect people and equipment first, then document the leak with photos, times and weather. Check for clogged drains and ponding water, which cause many flat-roof leaks. If the roof is under a manufacturer or contractor warranty, call the warranty holder before anyone else works on it, so the warranty isn't voided. Water travels under membranes, so the leak inside is often not directly under the hole.

## First hour

- Move people and equipment, and cut power to anything wet if it's safe to do so.
- Contain water with buckets, tarps and plastic sheeting.
- Photograph the ceiling, floor, and any staining; note the time and the weather.
- If it's safe, have maintenance staff check that roof drains and scuppers aren't clogged.

## Finding the source

- Common culprits: clogged drains, seams, flashing at walls and curbs, HVAC units, pitch pans and roof edges.
- Ponding water that sits more than a couple of days after rain stresses membranes and seams.
- Infrared or electronic leak detection can locate wet insulation and breaches without tearing up the roof.

## Warranty and insurance

- Check whether the roof has a manufacturer warranty and a separate contractor workmanship warranty. Many require that only authorized contractors make repairs.
- Storm-related leaks may be covered by property insurance. Document everything and notify your carrier promptly. See roof insurance claims.

## Preventing the next one
Twice-yearly inspections and after-storm checks catch most problems early. Use our commercial roof maintenance checklist.

## Related guides
Commercial roof maintenance checklistCommercial roofing: free inspections and quotesRoof leaking? What to do right nowCommercial roof warranties: manufacturer vs. contractor

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does my flat roof leak only sometimes?
Leaks that appear with wind-driven rain or heavy storms often come from flashing, edges or HVAC curbs. Leaks after any rain often point to drains, seams or punctures.

### Is the leak above where the water drips?
Not always. Water can travel across the deck or through insulation before it shows up inside.

### Should I call the original installer?
If the roof is under warranty, yes. Repairs by others can void some warranties.

### How fast should a commercial leak be fixed?
As soon as possible. Wet insulation loses value and can lead to deck rust or rot and mold.

Commercial roofing

# Commercial roof warranties: manufacturer vs. contractor
A commercial roof warranty is only as useful as its fine print. Here's what the common types cover.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Commercial roofs usually carry two kinds of warranty. A manufacturer warranty covers materials and, in the stronger "system" or "no dollar limit" (NDL) versions, the cost of repairing leaks caused by materials or installation, for a set number of years. A contractor workmanship warranty covers installation errors, often for a shorter period. Read both, since exclusions and maintenance requirements decide whether they pay.

## Common warranty types

Type | Usually covers | Watch for | 

Material-only | Defective membrane or components | May not cover labor to fix leaks | 

System / NDL | Leak repairs from materials or workmanship, no dollar cap | Requires approved contractor, specific materials and a final inspection | 

Contractor workmanship | Installation mistakes | Often shorter; only as good as the contractor's staying power | 

## What commonly voids or limits coverage

- Repairs or new penetrations by unauthorized contractors.
- Skipped maintenance, like clogged drains or debris left on the roof.
- Damage from foot traffic, other trades or rooftop equipment.
- Severe weather beyond stated wind speeds; check the wind rating.
- Not registering the warranty or paying the issuing fee.

## Tips before you sign

- Ask for a sample warranty document from the manufacturer, not a brochure.
- Confirm the term, wind speed rating and whether it transfers if you sell.
- Keep inspection and maintenance records on file.

Homeowner version: residential roof warranties.

## Related guides
Commercial roofing: free inspections and quotesCommercial roof maintenance checklistRoof warranties explainedTPO vs. EPDM vs. PVC: which flat roof membrane is best?

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an NDL roof warranty?
No Dollar Limit: a manufacturer system warranty that pays for covered leak repairs without a cap on the dollar amount, for its term.

### Who issues a commercial roof warranty?
The membrane manufacturer issues the material or system warranty; the installing contractor issues the workmanship warranty.

### Does maintenance affect my roof warranty?
Often yes. Many warranties require reasonable maintenance and may exclude damage from clogged drains or debris.

### Can I transfer a commercial roof warranty?
Some are transferable with notice and a fee. Check the terms before you sell.

Homeowner guide

# HOA and condo roof replacement: a guide for boards
Replacing roofs across a community is a big project. Here's how boards and managers keep it organized and fair.
Updated November 18, 2026 · By the Bedrock Roof team

 Quick answer: Start with your governing documents to see whether the association or individual owners are responsible for roofs. Use a reserve study and a professional roof assessment to plan timing and budget. Then bid the work with one written scope, check licenses and insurance, and communicate the schedule clearly to owners. Many associations phase replacements over several years to match reserves.

## 1. Know who is responsible
CC&Rs and bylaws decide whether the association or each owner maintains and replaces roofs, and state law can affect this, especially for condominiums. If it's unclear, ask the association's attorney before bidding.

## 2. Plan with data

- A reserve study estimates when roofs will need replacing and how much to set aside.
- A roof condition assessment by a qualified roofer or consultant ranks buildings by need, with photos.
- Phasing the worst roofs first can spread cost and avoid special assessments.

## 3. Bid it right

- Write one scope: materials, colors approved by the architectural committee, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, cleanup and warranty.
- Get at least three bids from licensed, insured roofers. Ask for references from other communities.
- Confirm who pulls permits and how damage to landscaping, cars and gutters is handled.

## 4. Communicate with owners
Send schedules and notices well ahead: which buildings, which days, parking changes, noise hours, and who to call with concerns. Ask owners to move vehicles and fragile items from walls during tear-off.

## 5. Insurance and storms
After hail or wind, check the master policy and deductibles before signing anything. Be wary of contractors going door-to-door asking individual owners to sign. See roofing scams and insurance claims.

## Related guides
Commercial roofing: free inspections and quotesHow to read and compare roofing estimatesDoes insurance cover roof replacement?How to choose a roofer you can trust

## Frequently asked questions

### Who pays for roof replacement in an HOA?
It depends on the governing documents and state law. In many condominiums the association pays from reserves; in many single-family HOAs owners pay.

### Does an HOA need multiple roofing bids?
Many boards get at least three, and some governing documents or state laws require competitive bidding for large projects.

### Can an HOA require a specific roof color or material?
Usually, through architectural guidelines, though some states limit restrictions on certain materials like solar or impact-resistant shingles.

### How long does a community roof project take?
Each building often takes a few days, weather permitting. A whole community may be phased over weeks or years.

FAQ

# Questions homeowners ask
Straight answers about how Bedrock Roof works.

## All questions

### Is Bedrock Roof free for homeowners?
Yes. You never pay Bedrock Roof anything. Roofing contractors may pay us for introductions, which is how we keep the service free for you.

### Is Bedrock Roof a roofing company?
No. We are a referral service. We don't install or repair roofs. We connect you with an independent local roofing contractor, and any work is between you and that contractor.

### How many roofers will contact me?
We try to match each request with one local roofer instead of sending your number to a long list of companies. You can always get more quotes on your own, and we recommend at least two or three for a full replacement.

### Do I have to hire the roofer?
No. The inspection and quote are free and there's no obligation to hire anyone.

### Do you help with commercial roofs?
Yes. Owners and managers of commercial buildings, apartments, condos and HOAs can request a free inspection and quote from an independent commercial roofer. See our commercial roofing guide.

### Which areas do you serve?
Homeowners anywhere in the United States can send a request. If we can't find a roofer serving your ZIP code, we'll tell you.

### Can a roofer help with an insurance claim?
Many roofers will document storm damage with photos and a written estimate you can give your insurer. Whether a claim is covered is up to your insurance company, and nobody can promise approval.

### What happens after I submit the form?
We pass your request to an independent roofer serving your ZIP code, who will call or text you to set up a free inspection.

### Is the inspection really free?
Roofers in our referrals offer free inspections and quotes for homeowners who request them. If a roofer ever asks to charge you for an inspection, you're free to say no.

### Do you check roofers' licenses and insurance?
Roofers are independent businesses and we don't guarantee their work. Always verify the license with your state or local licensing board and ask for current insurance certificates before you sign. Our checklist shows you how.

### Will you sell my information?
We share your request only with the roofer we match you with so they can contact you about your roof. We don't sell your information to marketing lists. See our privacy policy.

### How do I stop calls or texts?
Reply STOP to any text, tell the caller you're no longer interested, or email hello@bedrockroof.com.

Trust

# Editorial policy
How we write and check the guides and city pages on Bedrock Roof.

## Who writes our content
Bedrock Roof's guides and city pages are written and edited by the Bedrock Roof team. We are a referral service, not a roofing contractor, so our guides explain how roofing, hiring and insurance usually work. They are not a substitute for an in-person inspection or for professional insurance or legal advice.

## How we research

- Costs come from published sources, which we name and link, such as Angi data reported by NerdWallet. We don't invent prices or averages.
- Licensing rules come from state licensing agencies. Rules change, so every page tells you to check the license with your state or city before hiring.
- City facts: population comes from GeoNames, climate type from the Köppen-Geiger classification, and county from U.S. Census boundaries. Local notes on storms and conditions are written by hand from public records and news coverage of major events.
- Insurance: we explain common policy terms. Your policy and insurer decide what's covered.

## What we won't publish

- Made-up reviews, testimonials, project photos or job counts.
- Claims that any roofer is licensed, insured or "certified" unless the homeowner can verify it.
- Promises about insurance approval.

## How we make money
Homeowners never pay us. Roofing contractors may pay us for introductions to homeowners who asked to be contacted. That doesn't change what our guides say. We recommend getting more than one quote and checking every contractor, including any we introduce you to.

## Corrections
If something on this site is wrong or out of date, email hello@bedrockroof.com. We review every report and update the page and its date when we make a change.

Last reviewed 2026-11-18.
